name: Concrete Materials Data Extraction Benchmark
description: This repository provides a human-annotated ground-truth benchmark for evaluating automated data extraction from tables and text in concrete materials literature. The benchmark contains 3,015 experimental records from 58 publications and is intended to support the evaluation and comparison of large language models and other automated data-extraction methods for converting information from scientific literature into structured materials data. The benchmark includes: Mixture proportions: cement, blast-furnace slag, fly ash, silica fume, calcined clay, limestone, other supplementary cementitious materials (SCMs) and their type, water, superplasticizer, coarse aggregate, and fine aggregate; Curing conditions: age, temperature, and relative humidity; Specimen dimensions: volume and aspect ratio; Mixture properties: compressive strength; and Source information: DOI of the original publication. Missing values are marked as null. The benchmark was developed as the human-annotated ground truth used to quantitatively evaluate the automated data-extraction pipeline reported in the associated publication, “Large language model-enabled automated data extraction for concrete materials informatics” (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41524-026-02304-6). The benchmark also served as a source for the companion Blended Cement Concrete Database (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18080350), which incorporates additional automatically extracted and subsequently curated records.
